489.history: The great western river port was Comhairle nam Mèinnean's gate to the western hills. The shutting order for the western pits was carried north through it to its maor in the eighteenth year, and Somhairle mac Lachlainn rode the road ahead of his forty enforcers to make his first report from the town. The enforcers' depot was built there in {{year:VI-0066}}: the priests of Òrd Mhanannain at the town's house refused to bless it, a young priest telling the captain that the house blessed a boat and a roof against the sea and the rain and would not pretend the same of a depot, and the roof was blessed at last by a stranger's hand. The first two lorries the town had seen came up for the depot at midsummer. Ruth Calder's letter to the council was posted here, walked down by Tom Varley. In the war the regiments came west by the western road to camp beside the enforcers, and An seachdamh rèisimeid was raised at the town, its rolls short of the order in its second week because the boats were still at sea, its maor said. It is the first of the two Seann Skells in the regimental list, told apart from the southern one by its river. In the present year the depot stands on its ground above the river as it was built, the regiments' lorries in its yard and Comhairle nam Mèinnean's tanks behind it, and the house of Manannan on the hill above it has not been asked again to bless it.
489.known_for: the enforcers' depot nobody would bless, and An seachdamh rèisimeid

47.history: The west-coast harbour of Òrd Mhanannain lay at the end of Slighe a' Ghuail's western branch. Comhairle nam Mèinnean's declaration that the western seams were the kingdom's, under Breith Leòid, went out through its offices in {{year:VI-0064}}. In the first month of the war Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn carried arms and dubhan to Seann Bhral by Slighe a' Ghuail, the yard at Muileann chrom loading day and night. The house of Manannan at Seann Bhral heard from its brothers at the western Seann Skell of their refusal to bless the depot, and sent them no word either way. Two brothers of the town who enlisted together died within the same hour of the same morning, and their names are on Clach nan Rèisimeidean. Slighe a' Ghuail's western branch ends at its harbour, and since the war the branch carries dubhan out to the western depots and nothing back; the town's own fishing boats took engines late, Òrd Mhanannain having been slow to bless them.
47.known_for: the western end of Slighe a' Ghuail, and its house of Manannan
